draft.title: Customers, suppliers and competitors
card: The market environment, also called the operating environment, is the part of the external environment closest to a business. It is made up of its customers, suppliers and competitors, and it affects that business directly.
the people or businesses who buy its products. Their needs and tastes decide what sells, so a business must keep track of what they want.
the businesses that provide its inputs, such as stock, materials or parts. They set the price, quality and timing of those inputs, which shape the business's costs and products.
other businesses selling similar products to the same customers. They push a business to improve its products or service, or to lower its prices.
draft.remember: Customers decide what sells, suppliers shape costs and quality, and competitors push a business to be better or cheaper.

a.q: Which of these shows competitors affecting a business?
opts: A rival cuts its prices, so the business offers a discount
Buyers lose interest in a product, so its sales fall
The cost of parts rises, so each product costs more
Stock arrives late, so customer orders are delayed
a.why: A rival selling similar products is a competitor, and its lower prices push the business to respond. Falling interest from buyers comes from customers, while the cost and timing of parts and stock come from suppliers.
a.clue: Look for another business selling to the same buyers.

b.q: Priya makes shirts in Ballarat. Her fabric supplier switches to a thinner cloth, and customers return shirts that tear. What caused the problem?
opts: Her supplier, through the quality of its inputs
Her customers, through a change in their tastes
b.why: The trouble starts with the fabric, an input whose quality is set by the supplier. The customers are reacting to faulty shirts, not changing what they like, so the returns are an effect rather than the cause.
b.clue: Trace the torn shirts back to where the problem began.

a.best: A rival cuts its prices, so the business offers a discount

b.best: Her supplier, through the quality of its inputs
